text:
Lina: Quick thought: what if we introduce a ONE-LINER deploy shorthand that expands to all the usual knobs (pinning, canary, change-window, preflight, rollback)? I'm tired of copying long examples into runbooks.
Marco: yes please. something like `deploy run cart-api@sha:abc1234 quick-window` and the bot expands it.
Priya: I prototyped a small helper that takes a profile name and emits a validated arglist + a checklist. works nicely for teams that want tighter defaults.
Alex: Needs to be safe for on-call. defaults should be conservative: canary=3%, auto-rollback-sla=true, snapshot-db=false unless explicitly asked.
Jordan: Proposal for syntax: `deploy now service=cart-api ref=sha:abc1234 profile=hotfix window=2026-03-23T01:00/02:00 note="fix double-charge" --preview`
Lina: Love the preview mode. release-bot could show the expanded command and a diff from the previous pinned manifest.
Marco: Also add a short alias `@fast` `@safe` etc that map to profiles. Keep mappings in infra/deploy-profiles.yaml so teams can override locally.
Priya: UX idea: `--edit-notes` opens a tiny modal form (title, summary, impact, rollback-instructions) and the bot autosaves it to the release note store. Saves the copy-paste.
Alex: For rollback, add `--escape` which is just a two-step confirm: mark previous version as promote, trigger promote job, then emit a short RC with `rollback: automated by --escape`. Minimal mental load for paging.
Jordan: Security/reg compliance: enforce `pin-reason` metadata when pinning longer than 24h for enterprise orgs. release-bot validation should block pin requests missing `pin-reason`.
Lina: Also want `--checkpoint` to snapshot DB migrations + schema hash to s3 before migrations start. Handy for schema rollbacks.
Marco: ops-bot integration: when `preflight=` is present, ops-bot posts a checklist in #deploys and waits for two approvals or `--auto-approve`. if `--preview` is used it only posts the checklist but doesn't block.
release-bot: noted: I can implement macro expansion + lint. would you prefer expansion happens client-side (cli) or server-side (bot)?
Priya: server-side is safer. fewer divergent clients. plus the bot can enforce policy (pin rules, metrics availability).
Alex: agree. Also expose `deploy lint` that checks metrics, infra pin compatibility, and whether the snapshot step will succeed.
Jordan: For auto-rollback thresholds: standardize on three metrics (p95 latency, 5xx rate, user-error-rate) and allow `rollback-policy=auto(thresholds=...)` with sane defaults.
Lina: I'll draft a tiny RFC: one-liner syntax, profiles yaml, server-side expansion, pin-reason enforcement for enterprise, `--checkpoint`, `--escape` rollback alias, and `--edit-notes` modal. Who wants to pick up which bits?
Marco: I'll own the expansion + bot linting.
Priya: I'll wire ops-bot checklist and notes modal tests.
Alex: I'll do the CLI alias and the `--escape` flow integration tests.
Jordan: I'll write the compliance checks around pin-reason and long-term pinned state.
release-bot: I'll add a preview expansion endpoint and a dry-run that emits the post-checklist payload.
Lina: Great. I'll open a draft PR with a PoC `deploy profiles` yaml and one sample `runbook snippet` to paste into docs. We'll iterate from there. :shipit:
